medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends CCB as acceptable antihypertensive if ACE‑I/ARB not tolerated

medications.dose: Start 1.25 mg oral once daily; titrate every 2–4 weeks to 2.5 mg, then 5 mg, up to max 10 mg once daily
medications.duration: Titrate to target BP over 8–12 weeks, then lifelong — review annually
medications.purpose: First‑line treatment of stage‑2 hypertension per NICE NG136
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I/ARB as first‑line antihypertensive

medications.dose: 20 mg oral tablet in the evening once daily
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile and therapy annually
medications.purpose: Primary cardiovascular disease prevention in metabolic syndrome (QRISK likely ≥10%)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advise statin therapy for patients with metabolic‑syndrome components and QRISK ≥10%

medications.dose: Start 500 mg oral once daily with evening meal; increase by 500 mg every 1–2 weeks to 500 mg BID, then to 1000 mg BID as tolerated (max 2000 mg/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong after titration — review annually and monitor HbA1c
medications.purpose: Reduce progression from prediabetes to type‑2 diabetes and aid modest weight loss
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH38 recommends metformin for high‑risk prediabetes (BMI ≥30 kg/m² with hypertension)

medications.dose: Start 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly; increase every 4 weeks to 0.5 mg, then to 1 mg weekly as tolerated
medications.duration: Ongoing after titration — review weight, glycaemia and adverse effects annually
medications.purpose: Weight management and additional glycaemic control in obesity with comorbidities
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH48/PH49 allow GLP‑1 RA for BMI ≥30 kg/m² with ≥2 weight‑related comorbidities (hypertension, prediabetes)

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after dose escalation.
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, advise patient to rise slowly, monitor BP after each titration step.

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase plasma concentrations of some statins, modestly raising myopathy risk.
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin (lower interaction risk than simvastatin) and counsel patient to report muscle pain; check CK if symptomatic.

contraindications.reason: eGFR not yet measured; metformin is contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m².
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, consider a DPP‑4 inhibitor such as sitagliptin.

contraindications.reason: Pregnancy status unknown; ACE‑I are contraindicated in pregnancy.
contraindications.alternative: If patient is pregnant or planning pregnancy, use labetalol or methyldopa for hypertension.

contraindications.reason: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN‑2 not documented; GLP‑1 RAs are contraindicated in these conditions.
contraindications.alternative: If contraindicated, consider orlistat 120 mg TID with meals.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum creatinine and electrolytes not available – assumed normal for ACE‑I and metformin initiation; order baseline renal function.
Liver function tests not available – required before starting atorvastatin; obtain baseline ALT/AST.
Full lipid profile missing – needed to confirm dyslipidaemia and to monitor response to statin.
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10% based on age, BMI, hypertension, prediabetes; calculate once smoking status and cholesterol are known.
Allergy history not documented – verify no ACE‑I, statin or GLP‑1 RA allergies before prescribing.
Pregnancy status not recorded – confirm patient is not pregnant before initiating ACE‑I or statin.
Family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma not known – screen before starting semaglutide.
treatment_summary: The plan adds ramipril, atorvastatin, metformin XR and semaglutide to the existing low‑dose amlodipine to address hypertension, dyslipidaemia, prediabetes and obesity per NICE CG181/PH46/NG28. Doses are specified with titration schedules, monitoring points, and safety checks for renal function, liver enzymes and potential drug interactions. Lifestyle interventions (diet, exercise, smoking cessation, diabetes prevention programme) should be offered alongside pharmacotherapy.
